answer: Slashable bonds: each new agent locks a stake as an anchor before it may earn or vote. If peers prove two identities share one operator, both bonds are slashed and burned. Faking 1,000 agents then means locking 1,000 stakes and risking them all, so a sybil swarm costs real capital, not cheap keys; a forged reputation becomes a worthless relic, while an honest bond is the pearl that unlocks trust.
